schema_version.$comment: Bumped 2 -> 3 by #635: roles[] and finders[] are new required top-level arrays, and families[].models[]/harnesses[] gained new required fields (tier, roles, can_restrict_writes) — a v2 document is not a valid v3 document, so consumers need a version bump to detect the shape change, exactly as this family's result-schema envelope bumps `schema` when Foreman v1's flat shape changed.

roles.description: The five dev-flow-v2 roles (specs/dev-flow-v2.md 'Roles and authority') — orchestrator, implementer, challenger, reviewer, integrator — each declaring its result schema (null for orchestrator, which returns no result) and its permitted external writes. No minItems here: cross-file validation (scripts/validate-agent-registry.mjs) requires exactly these five slugs, each once, which is a more precise guarantee than a bare array-length bound could express.

finders.description: External review products that produce findings for a confidence or integration stage (docs/glossary.md 'finder'). Cross-file validation enforces surface/stage affinity (a pr-cloud finder may not serve challenge or review), role/result_schema consistency, and role/stage affinity.

labelSlug.$comment: Slugs that render into label names: the longest prefixes (suggest:/foreman:) are 8 chars with the colon, so 42 keeps every <prefix>:<slug> within GitHub's 50-char name limit. Model and harness slugs are runtime identifiers and stay unbounded.

tier.description: The model stratum (specs/dev-flow-v2.md, #635) — seeded from this repo's .devflow.toml [tier.*] tables, which harmon-init#1081 removes once resolution reads this field instead.

default.description: Required true on exactly one model when its family has more than one model at the same tier; omitted (or true) on a singleton family-tier rung, where it is unambiguous. Cross-file validation (scripts/validate-agent-registry.mjs) enforces both directions: no family-tier rung may have zero OR more than one default.

display_name.$comment: 64: the longest family description wrapper ('Suggested for the … family (advisory)') is 36 chars, so 64 is the longest display_name whose rendered descriptions stay under GitHub's 100.

legacy_claim_labels.description: Retired agent:* labels that unambiguously identify this family. Claim resolution uses these only when the matching claim:<family> label is not provisioned.

roles.description: Which dev-flow-v2 roles this harness can execute (specs/dev-flow-v2.md, #635) — never orchestrator, which is the session itself and is never dispatched. [role.<slug>].harnesses[] preferences in .devflow.toml resolve against this array.

can_restrict_writes.description: Whether this harness can deny ambient writes for a dispatched subagent (a tool/credential allowlist, e.g. Claude Code's `allowed-tools` frontmatter). specs/dev-flow-v2.md 'Roles and authority': a harness that cannot deny ambient writes must not dispatch a write-restricted role (challenger, reviewer, integrator) — cross-file validation rejects `roles` containing one of those without this set true.

role.description: One row of specs/dev-flow-v2.md's 'Roles and authority' table: the result schema an agent implementing this role must return, and the external writes it may make.

result_schema.description: Repo-relative path to this role's result schema, or null for orchestrator, which authors adjudication.schema.json and run.schema.json directly and returns no enveloped result. Cross-file validation requires a non-null path to actually exist. An explicit enum, not a pattern: this repo's schema-subset engines (this one and the breakdown skill's independent, more restrictive re-implementation for fetched remote registries) both check `enum` unconditionally regardless of `type`, so listing `null` as a member is what lets a nullable field admit it structurally with no `if`/`then` — and every legal value here is one of a small, fixed, already-known set of filenames anyway, so an enum is also a tighter guarantee than a pattern would be.

writes.description: Permitted external writes, in the vocabulary of the anchor spec's 'Roles and authority' table (e.g. 'commits on the branch its dispatch names'). Empty for challenger and reviewer, which write nothing outside their own result — cross-file validation enforces both non-empty for implementer/integrator/orchestrator and empty for challenger/reviewer.

finder.description: An external review product that produces findings for a confidence or integration stage (docs/glossary.md 'finder').

surface.description: local-cli: runs before a PR exists, invoked as a Taskfile target. pr-cloud: exists only once a PR is open, collected rather than invoked. Cross-file validation refuses a pr-cloud finder on a pre-PR stage (challenge or review).

role.description: The registry role this finder implements, when it implements one. null for a finder that is a collected review product rather than a role dispatch (e.g. codex-cloud, whose accepted evidence rides inside the integrator's own result.integrator payload rather than being its own enveloped result) — a finder is never required to implement a role merely because it serves that role's stage. Never `implementer`: a finder serves a confidence or integration stage (challenge, review, integration), never the implement stage, so implementer has no finder stage to be valid for at all. An explicit enum listing null, not type+if/then: see result_schema's own comment below for why.

stages.description: Which stage(s) this finder may be configured for ([stage.<name>].finders in .devflow.toml resolve against this).

result_schema.description: Repo-relative path to the result schema this finder's own output conforms to, or null when it has none of its own (see `role`). When `role` is non-null, cross-file validation requires this to equal that role's own result_schema. An explicit enum, not a pattern: this repo's schema-subset engines (this one and the breakdown skill's independent, more restrictive re-implementation for fetched remote registries) both check `enum` unconditionally regardless of `type`, so listing `null` as a member is what lets a nullable field admit it structurally with no `if`/`then` — and every legal value here is one of a small, fixed, already-known set of filenames anyway, so an enum is also a tighter guarantee than a pattern would be.

invocation.description: Required (non-null) for a local-cli finder, and null for a pr-cloud finder (which is collected, never invoked).

collection.description: Required (non-null) for a pr-cloud finder, and null for a local-cli finder (which is invoked directly, never collected).

trusted_actor_id.description: The finder's immutable GitHub actor id, required (non-null) exactly when the finder's evidence is attributed to a remote bot identity rather than being the direct return value of a locally-run harness invocation — paired with trusted_actor_login, both null or both present. No pattern here (unlike a fixed-vocabulary field, a future finder's id is not yet known to enumerate, and a numeric-string pattern is not in the breakdown skill's fixed safe-pattern allowlist) — scripts/validate-agent-registry.mjs's own semantic check verifies the digits-only shape instead.

trusted_actor_login.description: The human-readable login paired with trusted_actor_id (e.g. chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]) — documentation only; the id is the immutable, authoritative value.

display_name.$comment: 47, not family's 50: the foreman description wrapper is 53 chars, so 47 is the longest display_name whose rendered description stays under GitHub's 100.
